title: harden diarization so failures land the session as DIARIZATION_FAILED instead of crashing
description: After the first recording on a fresh install, the post-stop diarization step crashes the app instead of labelling speakers. The crash is unrecoverable from Kotlin's point of view: either a native SIGSEGV inside `OfflineSpeakerDiarization.process(...)`, an OOM during reading the WAV into a `FloatArray`, or a hang that the user perceives as a crash. Fix is defensive on three fronts: bound the diarization to a 30-minute wall-clock timeout, catch every `Throwable` (including `Error` subtypes the use case already swallows) and pin a clear `DIARIZATION_FAILED` status with a useful message, and ensure `RecordingService.handleStop()` releases the foreground state even if the use case never returns. Tests cover every failure path through fakes, no native calls.
steps: * Wrap the body of `run(sessionId, onProgress)` in `coroutineScope { withTimeoutOrNull(DIARIZATION_TIMEOUT_MS) { ... } ?: handleTimeout(sessionId) }`. The timeout is `const val DIARIZATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 30L * 60L * 1_000L`. `handleTimeout` is a small private helper that logs `Log.w(TAG, "diarization timed out for session $sessionId after ${DIARIZATION_TIMEOUT_MS}ms")`, sets the status to `DIARIZATION_FAILED` and returns `Unit`. The wrapping `coroutineScope` propagates a clean CancellationException on parent cancel; the `withTimeoutOrNull` swallows only the *timeout* race and lets cooperative cancels propagate normally. The timeout race IS a CancellationException under the hood — `withTimeoutOrNull` distinguishes via its boolean return so we never accidentally swallow a real cancel.

* Change the existing top-level `catch (t: Throwable)` to also log the throwable's full stack via `Log.w(TAG, "Diarization failed for session $sessionId", t)` (we already log the message; flip to passing the throwable so the user's bug reports carry the cause). The `Throwable` catch is left in place because it is the last-resort safety net for synchronous errors before `withContext` runs the diarizer.

* Add a `private fun handleFailure(sessionId: Long, where: String, t: Throwable)` that logs `Log.w(TAG, "diarization failed: $where session=$sessionId", t)` and flips status to `DIARIZATION_FAILED`. Use it from both the timeout path and the catch path so the log line is uniform.

* Make the optional `computeLabels` (the speaker-embedding pass) cap at `EMBED_TIMEOUT_MS = 60L * 1_000L` (60 s). The user already grants 3 s of audio for the minimum; embedding a 30 s window should be well under that, and the cap is a safety net for a runaway model.

* Refactor `handleStop()` so the foreground tear-down is in a `try { ... } finally { releaseWakeLock(); ServiceCompat.stopForeground(this@RecordingService, ServiceCompat.STOP_FOREGROUND_REMOVE); stopSelf() }` block. The try-block launches `controller.stop()`, runs the diarization use case, and either succeeds or times out; the finally-block always tears the foreground down. Move `releaseWakeLock()` *before* `ServiceCompat.stopForeground(...)` so the wake lock is gone before the FGS state flips (matches the existing release ordering in `handleStart` and the error latch in `startStateObserver`).

* Handle the `diarizeUseCase()` call so it cannot throw. Wrap the body in `scope.launch { runCatching { diarizerUseCase().run(completedId) }.onFailure { Log.w(TAG, "post-stop diarization threw", it); repository.setStatus(completedId, SessionStatus.DIARIZATION_FAILED) } finally { tear down foreground } }`.

* The service therefore gets a `repository: SessionRepository` field. Resolve it via `container` (the existing `(application as ConvoApp).container.sessionRepository` pattern). Inject it through a `RecordingService.repository: SessionRepository` getter that's defensive if the container isn't ready (it always is at this point in the lifecycle, but defensive nullability keeps Robolectric and the auto-instantiated service happy).

`app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`: add `session_status_diarization_failed` ("Identifying speakers failed") used by the session-detail screen status banner (the existing banner already renders whatever string the status maps to).

* `app/src/test/java/com/convoscribe/diarization/DiarizeSessionUseCaseTest.kt`: add (a) `run_diarizerFactoryThrows_setsStatusToFailed` — a fake diarizer factory that throws `OutOfMemoryError("simulated OOM")`; assert the session row lands at `DIARIZATION_FAILED` after the call returns; assert the use case does NOT rethrow. (b) `run_diarizerFactoryCompletesButReadingSamplesThrows_setsStatusToFailed` — throw `IOException("bad WAV")` from the `readSamples` lambda; assert `DIARIZATION_FAILED`. (c) `run_veryLongRunningDiarizer_timesOut` — a fake diarizer whose `diarize()` calls `Thread.sleep(31 * 60 * 1000)` (shorter in tests via a `delay()` injected through an `ApproachDelayProvider` lambda parameter, default `delay(...)`); assert the call returns inside 1 second of the test deadline, session is `DIARIZATION_FAILED`. Use `kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest` with a virtual-clock so the test is fast. (d) `run_cancellationPropagatesCleanly` — parent launch cancels mid-diarization; assert `CancellationException` propagates, session row is left at `DIARIZING` (recovery picks it up).

* `app/src/test/java/com/convoscribe/service/RecordingServiceTearDownTest.kt` (new): use a Robolectric `ServiceController<RecordingService>` and a fake `AppContainer` so the tear-down path can be exercised. Two cases: (a) `handleStop_withSucceedingDiarization_releasesForegroundAfterCompletion`; (b) `handleStop_withHangingDiarization_releasesForegroundAfter30Minutes` (the test uses an injected `clock`-style seam that the timeout can be pinned to a 0 ms wait so the test finishes in milliseconds while still exercising the same code path).
* Defensive: extract `RecordingService.diarizationTimeoutMs()` as an `@VisibleForTesting` package-internal function with a `var override: Long? = null` so tests can pin it without forking the class.
acceptanceCriteria: Calling `DiarizeSessionUseCase.run` with a diarizer that throws `OutOfMemoryError` lands the session in `DIARIZATION_FAILED` and never rethrows

Calling `DiarizeSessionUseCase.run` with a diarizer that takes longer than 30 minutes (under a virtual clock this is configurable, default 30 min) lands the session in `DIARIZATION_FAILED` and returns inside the test deadline

Calling `DiarizeSessionUseCase.run` and cancelling the parent coroutine mid-diarization propagates the `CancellationException` and leaves the session row at `DIARIZING` (the recovery pass picks it up)
`RecordingService.handleStop()` releases the wake lock and removes the foreground notification even when the diarization use case never returns
Existing `DiarizeSessionUseCaseTest` cases still pass (the happy path + zero-segment path + embedding-failure path are untouched)
`source scripts/env.sh && ./gradlew ktlintCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug` exits 0

`docs/MANUAL_TEST.md` §6 (Post-stop diarization) gains a one-line note: "If speaker labels never appear within 30 minutes, the session is automatically marked Identifying-speakers-failed; tap Retry Identifying speakers in the session overflow menu to rerun."
notes: Files to read first: `diarization/DiarizeSessionUseCase.kt`, `service/RecordingService.kt`, `recording/SessionRecovery.kt`, the existing `DiarizeSessionUseCaseTest.kt`. The 30-min timeout is conservative: real diarization on a 10-minute recording takes under a minute on the Q-6690, and 60 minutes on a 60-minute recording. 30 minutes gives a ~3-4× safety margin for the Onyx Boox e-ink BSP without leaving the user waiting forever. The native crash case (SIGSEGV from the JNI side) cannot be caught from Kotlin — the timeout + foreground-tear-down watchdog covers the closest equivalent: a hang. A future task can split the diarization into a separate process if real SIGSEGV crashes persist. Never instantiate `com.k2fsa.sherpa.onnx` engine classes in tests. Always: run `source scripts/env.sh` before Gradle; the verify command is `source scripts/env.sh && ./gradlew ktlintCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug`; run `./gradlew --stop` before ending.
